diffuseAlbedo.source: Palette.json: accent.giallo-siena realMaterial (yellow brecciated marble, Montagnola Senese)
diffuseAlbedo.note: A straw yellow from the iron hydroxide (limonite) staining the calcite, read from trade photographs; to be measured on a specimen.

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.source: Granital Siena s.r.l., 'Cave di marmo Giallo Siena: Giallo Siena Broccatello' data sheet (A.D. Arianna Losi, Marzo 2013; tests at the Marble Laboratory, Politecnico di Torino), physical-mechanical table: EN 1936-07 open porosity 0.24 % (st. dev. 0.09); EN 13755-08 water absorption 0.10 % (0.01); EN 1936-07 apparent density 2710 kg/m3, http://www.granitalsiena.com/pdf/giallo-siena-broccatello-marmo-granital-siena.pdf
porosity.note: Verified on the Broccatello variety from Sovicille (Siena). The macroscopic description reads 'The rock is compact but porous near the veins'. I did not open the Lithos Design listing, so it is dropped.

wettingDepth.source: Palette.json: accent.giallo-siena realMaterial (yellow brecciated marble, Montagnola Senese)
wettingDepth.note: As the Crema Marfil: a dense stone wets only its outer millimetre.

grain.source: Granital Siena s.r.l., 'Giallo Siena Broccatello' data sheet (2013), microscopic description (EN 12407 and EN 12670): calcite > 95 % in straight anhedral crystals; 'The crystals vary from 60 to 900 um in some veins and patches of the mosaic'; macroscopic: 'medium-fine-grained', http://www.granitalsiena.com/pdf/giallo-siena-broccatello-marmo-granital-siena.pdf
grain.note: Accepted with a caveat. The sheet's sentence (Italian: 'variano da 60 a 900 um in alcune venature e plaghe del mosaico') can be read as giving the range only for some veins and patches. The size of the bulk mosaic may be narrower. The sheet calls the stone a banded, foliated calcitic crystalloblastic marble, with quartz blasts (< 0.8 mm), limonite, hematite, chlorite, acicular muscovite and tourmaline at the veins.
grain.derivation: Geometric mean of the stated crystal-size range: sqrt(0.06 mm x 0.9 mm) = 0.232 mm

bed.source: Palette.json: accent.giallo-siena realMaterial (yellow brecciated marble, Montagnola Senese)
bed.note: The breccia's clasts and their darker seams, a first size read from trade photographs.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.
